From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller has tagged almost every position **[STANDARD]** and says these were "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the parties have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have treated all of this as open.** These are the Seller's drafting positions, not agreed terms. Nothing in the material shows Buyer agreement, and several of the "standard" items are among the most Buyer-adverse in the package.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] also says the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement." Please confirm with the deal team that no one has agreed any of these points. If someone has, we need to see that correspondence.

---

## A. Limitation and liability regime

### 1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties under the general cap and time limit (reject)
- The proposal puts title and capacity under a 20% cap (AUD 4.8m), an 18-month time limit and the AUD 25k / AUD 250k thresholds. If the Seller does not own the shares, or cannot sell them, we lose the whole AUD 24m. Recovery would be capped at a fifth of that and would expire in 18 months.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept this. It departs from market practice.
- **Push back:**
  - Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of the price.
  - Time limit of at least 6–7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - No de minimis or basket for these warranties.

### 2. Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) (reject)
- As drafted, the cap, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions would also cover fraud, specific indemnities, tax claims, leakage or price-adjustment claims, and breaches of covenants and completion obligations. Specific indemnities are worth little if they sit inside a 20% cap and an 18-month window and only pay above a AUD 250k basket.
- **Push back:** carve the following out of all limitations:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (see below);
  - covenants, completion obligations and price-adjustment mechanics.
- Exclusive remedy must not cut down termination rights, specific performance or injunctions.
- Non-reliance must be limited to pre-contract statements outside the SPA and disclosure. It must exclude fraud. Note that contracting out of s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law is generally ineffective, though non-reliance wording can still affect causation arguments. We should not let the drafting imply a broader exclusion.

### 3. General cap (20%), thresholds and 18 months (negotiable)
- These numbers are within a commercial range for general warranties but sit at the Seller-friendly end.
- **Push back:**
  - Cap of 30–50%, or 100% if we are not taking W&I insurance.
  - The basket should be a "tipping" basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded), not an excess-only deductible.
  - De minimis of around AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
  - Time limit of 24 months for general warranties, so we get at least two audit cycles.
- If W&I insurance is in play, align these settings with the policy.

### 4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (reject)
- **Tax:**
  - A standalone, dollar-for-dollar tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax.
  - Tax claims capped at 100% of the price.
  - A time limit that runs past the ATO amendment period, generally 4 years for a company of this type, plus a buffer. Confirm the applicable period with tax advisers.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay issue (item 9), treat IP ownership warranties as quasi-fundamental. That means a higher cap and a longer period.

---

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

### 5. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (Schedule 7, DL [1.1]–[1.2]) (reject)
- Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, plus statutory registers, the Accounts and all public records, would hollow out the warranties. In effect, the Seller warrants only what we could not have found anywhere.
- **Push back:**
  - Disclosure is effective only if it is **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** to let a reasonable buyer identify the nature and scope of the matter, and only **against the specific warranty** it qualifies.
  - No general disclosure of the data room. At most, the data room can be deemed disclosed where it is fairly disclosed, under an agreed index delivered on USB at signing.
  - Public records limited to searches of the ASIC, PPSR and court registers on a fixed date before signing.
  - The Accounts are not a general disclosure.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
  - Any update to the Disclosure Letter between signing and Completion must not cure breaches. Material disclosures should instead give us a termination right.

### 6. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3) (reject)
- The clause covers "the Buyer or its advisers" and anything "discoverable". That is constructive knowledge, which goes further than general disclosure. It would turn our own diligence into a defence for the Seller. It also conflicts with DL [11], where the Seller admits the Buyer must still evaluate the matters.
- **Push back:**
  - Preferred position: knowledge does not affect claims (pro-sandbagging).
  - Fallback: limit it to **actual** knowledge of a short list of named Buyer deal-team individuals, and only of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Never include advisers' knowledge or "discoverable" matters.

---

## C. Specific transaction issues

### 7. Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue) (cl 3 / 6.3)
- The DL at [2] confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller's position has two problems:
  - It uses "reasonable endeavours", which is a weak obligation.
  - The condition would count as satisfied on delivery of "written consent". A consent that carries onerous conditions, such as repricing, a shorter term or new obligations, would still satisfy it.
- **Push back:**
  - A hard condition precedent: Bluefen's written consent, either unconditional or on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The condition is for the Buyer's benefit and only the Buyer can waive it.
  - "Best" or "all reasonable" endeavours on the Seller.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - A warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.
  - If the Buyer ever waives the condition to close, a price adjustment or retention tied to Bluefen revenue.

### 8. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m) (cl 2 / 7)
- A release "following Completion" is incompatible with a debt-free, cash-free deal. The facility has not been repaid and has not been discharged (DL [3]). The change-control clause (8.1) may also trigger default on Completion.
- Riverlark may hold security over the shares as well as the Company's assets, which would bear directly on title.
- **Push back:** at Completion, require:
  - a payout letter and a deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a fixed short period;
  - return of title documents;
  - release of any share security.
- Repay through the funds flow out of the price and treat it as Financial Indebtedness deducted dollar for dollar.
- Add a specific indemnity for any break costs or default interest.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The Company may therefore not own IP it uses.
- An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the debt but not the real risk, which is loss of IP ownership, infringement claims or re-licensing cost.
- **Push back:**
  - As Completion deliverables: evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, together with a signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, the AUD 180k is treated as Indebtedness, plus a retention.
  - A broad specific indemnity covering all loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials, outside the cap, basket and 18-month limit.

### 10. Completion bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) (funds flow)
- Calling the bonuses "a matter for the Seller" is wrong. They are Company liabilities triggered by the sale, and the Company will pay them after we own it.
- The DL at [5] is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and PAYG withholding. NSW payroll tax will likely apply. Whether super is payable depends on how the bonus is characterised, so tax advisers should confirm.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the AUD 420k plus all employer on-costs as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness, deducted from the price and paid through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Show the deduction in the funds flow.
  - Check whether any other change-of-control or retention payments exist.

### 11. DD-006 export and privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- A download link went to an unintended external address and potentially exposed about 1,240 records. As at 22 September the matter was still "preliminary". The Seller's view that it is "not expected to be material" is an assertion only. It gives us no protection.
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity covered by the Privacy Act must generally assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. Given today's date, we should ask why the assessment is not complete. Coverage, and the date the incident was discovered, need to be confirmed.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing: a full investigation report, the notification decision and supporting reasoning, and copies of any OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity, uncapped or separately capped and outside the basket and time limits, for all loss from the incident. That includes regulatory penalties to the extent the law permits indemnity, remediation, notification costs and third-party claims.
  - The incident disclosure must not qualify the privacy and data-security warranties for anything beyond its disclosed facts.
  - Consider a retention.

### 12. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- The DL at [8] tells us to read DD-008 and DD-011 together, and calls these "related" renewals. That raises two concerns:
  - The renewals may have been split to stay under an approval threshold.
  - The supplier may be a related party.
- The Seller does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Labelling them "ordinary course" does not make them so.
- **Push back:**
  - Seek confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller or management, the timing of each renewal, and the termination rights.
  - If any are related-party or outside the ordinary course, the Seller either terminates them before Completion at its own cost or bears them as Indebtedness or leakage.
  - Add a related-party warranty and a pre-Completion conduct covenant prohibiting new or renewed contracts above a threshold without Buyer consent.

### 13. Title (DD-012)
- A share register is the Company's own record and does not prove title on its own. The DL at [10] concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:**
  - Run our own checks: ASIC company extract and historical issued-share filings, constitution, share certificates, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, and any shareholder agreements or pre-emption rights.
  - Obtain full title and capacity warranties as fundamental warranties (item 1).
  - At Completion: executed transfers, share certificates, release of any encumbrance (including Riverlark), and waivers of any pre-emptive rights.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller says the lease needs only notification and that the Mossvale assignment restriction does not catch a share sale. Those are the Seller's readings.
- **Action:**
  - Have our team review the actual clauses, including any change-of-control definition or deemed-assignment wording.
  - Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
  - If Mossvale contains deemed-assignment language, add consent as a condition or obtain a specific indemnity.

### 15. "No admission" (DL [1.4])
- This is acceptable in principle. It must not dilute the specific facts disclosed, and it must not be read as qualifying any warranty or indemnity.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | "[STANDARD]" labels | Pre-agreed, no scrutiny | Treat everything as open; confirm nothing was agreed |
| 1 | Title and capacity warranties | 20% cap, 18 months | 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds |
| 2 | Limitations scope | All Claims | Carve out fraud, fundamental and tax warranties, indemnities, covenants and price mechanics |
| 3 | General warranties | 20% / AUD 25k / AUD 250k excess / 18 months | 30–50%, tipping basket, lower de minimis, 24 months (or align with W&I) |
| 4 | Tax and IP | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; longer tax period; IP quasi-fundamental |
| 5 | Disclosure | General data room and public records | Fair, specific disclosure only; agreed index; no updates curing breach |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | Constructive, includes advisers | Pro-sandbagging, or actual knowledge of named individuals only |
| 7 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Hard condition precedent, conditions acceptable to Buyer, walk right |
| 8 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Payout and release at Completion, deducted from price, PPSR discharge |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity for SOW3 payment only | Proof of payment and confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad IP indemnity |
| 10 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Seller's matter, not in funds flow | Deduct AUD 420k plus on-costs; specific indemnity |
| 11 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Full investigation and NDB assessment first; specific indemnity; retention |
| 12 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Related-party and splitting check; terminate or treat as debt; conduct covenant |
| 13 | Title | Register only | Independent verification; full title warranties; Completion deliverables |
| 14 | Lease and Mossvale | No consent needed | Our own clause review; notice or consent as Completion deliverables |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud and fundamental carve-outs, and the disclosure and knowledge framework (items 1, 2, 5, 6).
2. Riverlark, the bonuses and Ironquay as price and Completion mechanics (items 8–10).
3. Bluefen as a hard condition precedent (item 7).
4. Specific indemnities for DD-006 and Ironquay.
5. A retention or escrow, or W&I insurance, to support the indemnities.

**Next steps:**
- Prepare an issues list for the Seller marking all items as open.
- Request outstanding documents: Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout figures, Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 investigation report, and Sandbar party details.
- Instruct tax advisers on payroll tax and super for the bonuses, and on the tax indemnity period.

- A download link went to an unintended external address and potentially exposed about 1,240 records. As at 22 September the matter was still "preliminary". The Seller's view that it is "not expected to be material" is an assertion only. It gives us no protection.
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity covered by the Privacy Act must generally assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. Given today's date, we should ask why the assessment is not complete. Coverage, and the date the incident was discovered, need to be confirmed.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing: a full investigation report, the notification decision and supporting reasoning, and copies of any OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific indemnity, uncapped or separately capped and outside the basket and time limits, for all loss from the incident. That includes regulatory penalties to the extent the law permits indemnity, remediation, notification costs and third-party claims.
  - The incident disclosure must not qualify the privacy and data-security warranties for anything beyond its disclosed facts.
  - Consider a retention.

### 12. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- The DL at [8] tells us to read DD-008 and DD-011 together, and calls these "related" renewals. That raises two concerns:
  - The renewals may have been split to stay under an approval threshold.
  - The supplier may be a related party.
- The Seller does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Labelling them "ordinary course" does not make them so.
- **Push back:**

  - If any are related-party or outside the ordinary course, the Seller either terminates them before Completion at its own cost or bears them as Indebtedness or leakage.
  - Add a related-party warranty and a pre-Completion conduct covenant prohibiting new or renewed contracts above a threshold without Buyer consent.

### 13. Title (DD-012)
- A share register is the Company's own record and does not prove title on its own. The DL at [10] concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:**

  - Obtain full title and capacity warranties as fundamental warranties (item 1).
  - At Completion: executed transfers, share certificates, release of any encumbrance (including Riverlark), and waivers of any pre-emptive rights.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller says the lease needs only notification and that the Mossvale assignment restriction does not catch a share sale. Those are the Seller's readings.

  - Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
  - If Mossvale contains deemed-assignment language, add consent as a condition or obtain a specific indemnity.

### 15. "No admission" (DL [1.4])
- This is acceptable in principle. It must not dilute the specific facts disclosed, and it must not be read as qualifying any warranty or indemnity.
